symbol().details: Returns the symbol of the token.

totalSupply().details: Returns an indicator of the underlying encrypted total supply. The value is **not** the real total supply — it is a counter that starts at `7984.0000` on first mint and shifts by `0.0001` per mint/burn.

transferOwnership(address).details: Starts the ownership transfer of the contract to a new account. Replaces the pending transfer if there is one. Can only be called by the current owner. Setting `newOwner` to the zero address is allowed; this can be used to cancel an initiated ownership transfer.

underlying().details: Returns the address of the underlying ERC-20 token.

unshield(address,address,bytes32).details: Initiates an unshield of an encrypted `amount` from `from`, creating a pending unshield request for `to`. The caller must have ACL access to `amount` and must be `from` or an operator for `from`. Returns the encrypted amount that was burned.

unshield(address,address,uint64).details: Initiates an unshield of `amount` confidential tokens from `from`, creating a pending claim for `to`. The caller must be `from` or an operator for `from`. Returns the encrypted amount that was burned. The claim is keyed by a unique id — read it from {getClaim}/{getUserClaims}, NOT from the burned handle.

ClaimReassigned(bytes32,address,address).notice: Emitted when a pending claim is re-pointed at a new recipient.

getClaim(bytes32).notice: Pending-claim views, keyed by the unique claim id (NOT the ciphertext handle).

perUserShieldCap().notice: Max total USDC (underlying units) one address may ever shield, counted both for the address that pays and for the address credited. 0 = no deposits.

reassignClaim(bytes32,address).notice: Re-points an unsettled claim at `newTo`. Callable by the claim's current recipient or an operator acting for them. A claim's recipient is fixed at burn time and settlement pays that address unconditionally, so a recipient that cannot accept the payout — a contract with no payable fallback on a native wrapper, a blocklisted address on an ERC-20 wrapper — would otherwise strand the burned value in the wrapper forever (Consensys Diligence 5.13). Reassignment is the escape hatch: the value is already the recipient's, so only the recipient may redirect it. The claim keeps its id, so a decryption proof obtained before the reassignment stays valid.

renounceOwnership().notice: Disabled: without an owner, a pause could never be lifted.

shield(address,uint256).notice: Shield `amount` USDC into Private USDC for `to`, subject to the caps and the pause.

shieldedBy(address).notice: Lifetime USDC shielded by each depositor (public anyway: deposits are on-chain).

shieldedTo(address).notice: Lifetime USDC shielded to each recipient.

totalShieldCap().notice: Max USDC (underlying units) held for holders at once (deposits minus paid-out claims).

totalShielded().notice: USDC held for holders: counted deposits minus claimed payouts. Direct transfers to the contract are not counted, so they cannot be used to block deposits.

unshieldAll(address).notice: Unshield your entire confidential balance to `to`. Creates a pending claim like {unshield}; the amount becomes public when the claim is decrypted and paid out.

userdoc.notice: Confidential USDC for the Zon PayBox plugin. All money logic (shield, encrypted transfers, unshield, claim) is Fhenix's audited FHERC20ERC20Wrapper, used unchanged. This contract only adds launch guard rails:  - Deposit caps: a lifetime cap per depositor AND per recipient, and a cap on total USDC held.    The total is tracked internally, so USDC sent straight to the contract cannot fill the cap.  - Pause switch: stops NEW deposits only. Private sends, unshield and claim always work,    so a pause can never trap anyone's money.  - No admin withdraw: the owner can change caps and pause deposits. Nothing else.    There is no function that lets the owner, or anyone, move another person's funds.    Ownership cannot be renounced, so caps and pause can never be frozen without an owner.  - unshieldAll: lets a holder withdraw their whole confidential balance without first    having to decrypt it (recipients often don't know their exact balance).
